model_system: Acquired tamoxifen-resistant ER+ breast cancer model if available (e.g. a TAMR derivative of MCF-7/T47D, matching this project's own GSE118713/GSE240112 resistance-model framing); parental ER+ line as comparator
arms: (1) control; (2) tamoxifen (4-OHT); (3) USP34 inhibition [genetic: CRISPRi/shRNA/dominant-negative catalytic-dead C1903S, since no chemical probe exists yet -- see Part 2 verdict]; (4) USP34 inhibition + tamoxifen
readouts: viability (dose-response); apoptosis (Annexin V/caspase-3/7); clonogenic survival; ER signaling (ERE-luciferase reporter or ESR1 target-gene qPCR: TFF1/PGR/GREB1); USP34 mechanistic readout (AXIN1 ubiquitination status, active beta-catenin, RUNX2/Smad1 levels given the bone-pathway overlap); synergy/additivity analysis (e.g. Bliss independence) between arms 3 and 2 vs arm 4
normal_cell_comparator: Given the documented bone (PMID 30181118) and CNS-developmental (PMID 42315110) liabilities, and expression-only-but-unstudied muscle signal, include a normal-cell comparator arm: human primary MSCs undergoing osteogenic induction (direct extension of the existing Guo et al. 2018 assay) +/- the same USP34 perturbation, reading out osteogenic differentiation markers (RUNX2, ALP activity, mineralization) -- this directly tests whether the level of USP34 inhibition needed for a tamoxifen-sensitising cancer-cell effect also measurably impairs normal osteogenic differentiation, which is the central therapeutic-window question for USP34
open_question: No USP34 chemical probe exists, so any 'inhibition' arm must currently be genetic (CRISPRi/shRNA/catalytic-dead mutant), not pharmacological -- this is a real, disclosed limitation of the proposed experiment, not a design choice

model_system: Same ER+/tamoxifen-resistant model system as EXP-1, for direct comparability
arms: (1) control; (2) tamoxifen; (3) VEZF1 inhibition/CRISPRi; (4) VEZF1 inhibition/CRISPRi + tamoxifen
readouts: (A) direct cancer-cell effect (viability, apoptosis, clonogenic survival in arm 3 vs 1); (B) additional tamoxifen sensitisation (arm 4 vs 2 and vs 3); (C) interaction/synergy analysis distinguishing whether VEZF1 loss acts as a pure sensitiser, a direct cytotoxic hit, or both (testing the dual-action hypothesis directly) -- given VEZF1's 27.3% baseline ER+/luminal DepMap dependency, arm 3 alone is expected to show a measurable direct effect in a meaningful fraction of lines, which is itself a key confirmatory readout
normal_cell_comparator: Given the new cardiac-muscle finding (PMID 31911272), include primary human cardiomyocytes (or a zebrafish larval assay directly extending that paper's own model) as a comparator, reading out contractile function -- this is a materially different and arguably more urgent comparator than a generic normal-cell line, because it is the one system where a real, causal, postnatal VEZF1 loss-of-function phenotype has already been demonstrated
open_question: whether VEZF1's ER+/luminal DepMap dependency (arm 3's expected direct effect) is itself tamoxifen-context-independent or tamoxifen-context-dependent is not yet known and is a primary output of this experiment, not an input assumption

arms: (1) control; (2) tamoxifen; (3) TEAD1 inhibitor (existing clinical-stage TEAD auto-palmitoylation-pocket chemotype) alone; (4) TEAD1 inhibitor + tamoxifen
readouts: PRIMARY: does TEAD1 inhibition/knockdown reduce VEZF1 expression or VEZF1 target-gene activity (VEGFR2, TIMP3/MMP2, CITED2 repression) in ER+ breast cancer cells? This is the single most important unconfirmed link in this entire phase -- the VEZF1-TEAD1 biochemical relationship was demonstrated in cardiac/zebrafish tissue (PMID 31911272), NOT in breast cancer cells, so this experiment tests transferability before any therapeutic inference is drawn. SECONDARY (only if the primary readout is positive): viability, apoptosis, tamoxifen sensitisation (arms 3/4 vs 1/2)
normal_cell_comparator: not proposed at this stage -- this is explicitly a target-validation experiment (does the biochemical link hold in this cell type at all), which should precede any normal-tissue safety work for TEAD1 specifically
open_question: this experiment could just as easily falsify the TEAD1 hypothesis as confirm it -- that is the intended, appropriate outcome of a target-validation experiment, and the plan is written to be genuinely informative either way, not to presuppose a positive result
